messages.author: 881c51ed14655bd5
messages.subject: Customizing Patterns output ect and Wiki
parts:
I have been messing with knitr some more trying to get the output that I need.  My last blog post on r.andrewredd.us, the one on dostats package, was built with knitr using markdown.  I ran into a few problems with it.  First my site is configured to use GeSHI for highlighting R code wrapped in a <pre lang="r"> tag.  but I don't get that from knitr.  I do get some marked up code, but without the stylesheet is fairly useless.  

I was able to make a work around with using `render_gfm()` to get the "```r" syntax that I fed into pandoc that produced similar highlighted code but also included the stylesheet that I was able to configure on my server.  Neither of these are things that I particularly like.  I was trying to do several things that I have not been able to figure out. It would be great if we can figure out how to do these and put them up on the wiki on github for others.  I feel like the hooks, patterns, etc. are not documented enough to do this.

  1. Change the output format to do other things like <pre lang="r"> or output like pandoc format with carrying over attributes.(http://johnmacfarlane.net/pandoc/demo/example9/pandocs-markdown.html)
  2. Change the patterns to include other things such as  "```r" for markdown with eval=FALSE as the default so that "```r eval=T" is required for evaluating code.  To be more accurate to markdown the pattern should be something like "^`{3,}\s*r"
  3. Change the file extension defaults such as .rmd for r laced markdown.  I personally dislike the _knit_ pattern since with the tools I use on a daily basis that is hard to strip off where the extension is very easy to strip off.
It would be great if there were some examples in the wiki of how to do this, or at least somewhere.  Also the wiki would be a great place to collect these patterns for other document types so that people can build up a library.

-Andrew

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Customizing Patterns output ect and Wiki
parts:
1. should be easy; there is not much difference in using ```r or <pre
lang="r">, e.g. for R source code:

knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) paste("<pre lang='r'>",
x, "</pre>", sep = ""))

this will wrap up R code in <pre></pre>. Yes, I probably need to write
a concrete example. Notes taken at
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/147

2. the obstacle for me is that the patterns have to be as unique as
possible; ```r is more or less unique, but I'm worried about the
ending pattern ``` because in a document there may be other types of
code besides R; the other issue is how to write chunk options: we can
write ```r eval=F, echo=F; the pattern for chunk.begin in this case
would be like ```r(.*).

3. I do not like _knit_ either, but that is just for the case when you
do not specify the output filename. You can put all source files under
one directory, but write output in another directory, e.g. file
structure:

input/source.md
output/

I'm under output/ now, and I can run knit('../input/source.md', output
= 'source.md'). If you have multiple files, you can use a loop to
process them. Messing with file extensions is also a possible way to
go...

@Carl: render_foobar() does not involve with patterns; it usually only
takes care of how the output should be written, e.g. set 8 output
hooks

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Customizing Patterns output ect and Wiki
parts:
Yes that is what I called patterns, or syntax. If you guarantee
[/code] is used *only* for R code, basically this what you need:

knit_patterns$set(chunk.begin = '^\\[code lang="r", (.*)\\]',
chunk.end = '^\\[/code\\]')

I did not test them, though. There are patterns for other elements
such as inline R code; if you just want to borrow the syntax for HTML,
you can first

knit_patterns$set(all_patterns$html)

then change the two patterns above.

Regards,
Yihui
